## 開場固定收益主論點

油價衝擊不再局限於長端，而是直接進入美債殖利率曲線中對政策敏感的區段。2年期殖利率上升5個基點至4.39%，5年期上升6個基點至4.55%，漲幅超過10年期的4個基點至4.79%與30年期的2個基點至5.27%。這波熊市趨平令2s10s收窄1個基點至40個基點，2s30s收窄3個基點至88個基點。過去一週，2年期上升22個基點，相較之下10年期上升15個基點，30年期上升10個基點。投資人已不再把荷姆茲海峽周邊衝突再起只視為遠期通膨溢價，而是開始計入更迫近的聯準會政策後果。

各項價格變動的組合清楚顯示這項轉變。10年期實質殖利率持平於2.44%，10年期損益兩平通膨率則上升4個基點至2.35%。美國對伊朗發動新一輪打擊、德黑蘭報復，兩艘試圖駛離海峽的油輪又遭投射物擊中後，WTI期貨急升5.83%至$90.76，Brent上漲5.23%至$95.22。市場因而上調通膨補償，10年期實質折現率卻未進一步上升。地緣政治事件原本通常有利避險資產，但美元指數上升0.24%、黃金下跌1.21%，反而進一步凸顯預期政策利率走高的影響。

近期美國數據沒有為聯準會提供足以抵銷上述壓力的明確訊號。8月ISM製造業指數仍處擴張的54.6，但由55.6回落，低於55.2的市場共識，新訂單也放緩至53.7。支付價格指數仍高達71.1，供應商交貨指數升至59.3，延續能源、關稅與供應限制向近期通膨風險傳導的連結。職缺由718萬小幅增至727萬，略低於731萬的市場共識；聯準會理事Michael Barr則表示，若通膨未降溫，聯準會應果斷行動。這組訊號並不代表經濟全面加速，而是製造業動能放緩、勞動需求穩定與投入成本居高不下的不利組合，使9月升息仍有可能，卻非勢在必行。

風險資產雖已反映利率訊號，卻未顯現系統性壓力。S&P 500下跌0.71%，Nasdaq 100下跌1.29%，半導體指數下跌2.14%，VIX則收於16.34。美國投資級利差小幅擴大，高收益利差明顯擴大，硬通貨新興市場利差小幅擴大。這種分化至關重要：賣壓對存續期間與較低品質風險的傷害，大於對市場運作的干擾。30年期殖利率即使重返5.27%，過去一個月仍大致持平，因此不支持財政風險已失控的說法。較明確的結論是，新一輪油價升勢已將通膨不確定性轉化為更廣泛的緊縮衝擊；前端若要反轉，如今需要更弱的物價或勞動數據。

## 通膨訊號延伸至政策敏感期限

週二一連串數據呈現的聯準會難題，關鍵在訊號廣度，而非任何單一指標。製造業活動仍在擴張，但ISM回落、新訂單下降3點，顯示產業動能正在減速。同時，支付價格指數維持71.1不變，仍過高，無法支持單純的通膨降溫敘事。受訪企業指出，鋁、鋼、銅、電氣產品、燃料、記憶體產品與半導體均出現價格波動及成本上升，其中若干相同品項也傳出短缺。供應商交貨時間拉長，顯示價格壓力還涉及實體產能限制。因此，ISM整體指數放緩，並不具有需求轉弱且投入成本同步緩解時才會帶來的政策意涵。

近期其他指標也沒有化解這項歧義。物流經理人指數由68.9降至66.6，但仍穩居擴張區間。Redbook同店銷售年增率由9.1%加速至9.6%，是強勁的名目消費訊號；職缺也增加，儘管略低於預期。單看任何一項，都不足以證明經濟過熱；合併解讀則顯示，經濟活動尚未惡化到足以抵銷能源衝擊，而後者的傳導已反映在市場通膨補償。

Barr的發言也擴大了委員會內支持這項判斷的立場光譜。他認為，保持耐心的前提是有證據顯示通膨正朝2%降溫；若進展停滯，升息就是適當回應。這番話格外值得注意，因為Barr被視為立場相對中間的理事，而7月會議已有三票反對意見主張升息。期貨市場因而將9月15日至16日會議升息25個基點的機率定在接近70%。這是市場衡量值，不是政策承諾；新訂單放緩與價格高企並存，也說明為何機率分布中仍約有30%押注按兵不動。

長天期定價目前受兩項相互關聯的因素約束。30年期殖利率報5.27%，已回到財政部8月19日宣布擴大買回前夕的水準；10年期殖利率則較當時高出逾10個基點。相關操作預定9月9日展開，規模至少為先前的2倍，可支撐舊券流動性，卻無法自行降低民間投資人要求的通膨、財政或競爭性供給補償。IMF指出，全球公共債務正逼近GDP的100%；科技公司也持續為資本密集的AI建設融資。目前的熊市趨平顯示，聯準會反應函數主導每日的邊際定價；長債絕對殖利率仍高，則顯示結構性承接問題並未消失。

跨資產表現也界定了這項判斷的可信範圍。較高折現率壓抑長存續期間盈餘，半導體股跌幅超過大盤；美元與預期政策利率路徑走強，黃金也延續跌勢。股市波動率仍受控，S&P 500跌幅不到1%，顯示資本成本與資本配置正在重新定價，而非融資已經停擺。高收益利差擴大較為明顯，確實顯示較低品質借款人對同一總體衝擊的敏感度高於投資級發行人；個別信用債也比廣泛指數更清楚呈現這項差異。

## 日本突破3%，但政策掣肘未解

日本10年期殖利率自1996年以來首度升抵3%，不只是突破整數關卡。殖利率一度上升6個基點，約一年來已翻倍；2年期升至1.81%，5年期觸及2.265%的歷史高點，20年期升至3.885%，30年期則逼近約4.18%的歷史最高收盤水準。殖利率曲線同時重新計入日本央行近期升息與更高財政補償要求。這也改變銀行與壽險公司的相對價值判斷：國內公債目前提供的殖利率，足以涵蓋其資金與負債成本，而自1990年代以來的大部分時間都沒有這種機會。

10年期標售顯示，3%可以吸引需求，卻未建立可長久維持的上限。投標倍數由前次標售的2.56升至3.29，接近過去12個月平均的3.26；標售尾差收窄，MUFJ Morgan Stanley承接22%。相較前一週疲弱的2年期標售，這些結果證明平均殖利率逼近3%時，買盤確實進場。真正的保留在於各天期需求分布不均：投資人對基準天期依然要求3%以上的殖利率，而在週四30年期標售前，財政與存續期間風險更集中於30年期區段。

同一時段內，政策預期也更為強烈。美國財政部長Scott Bessent與日本央行總裁植田和男會面後，財政部表示，Bessent支持日本採取果斷的市場與貨幣政策措施，以處理日圓明顯低估，並將日圓走弱與國內通膨相連。會後說明也強調，政策溝通應穩定通膨預期並避免匯率過度波動。隔夜交換市場將日本央行在9月17日至18日會議升息的機率推至約99%，超過一個月前的2倍。

東京並未全盤接受華府的說法。日本財務大臣片山皋月否認曾與Bessent討論貨幣政策的執行，並強調日本央行的制度權限。儘管相關會談消息一度帶動日圓走強，美元兌日圓隨後仍突破160。日本前一個月已動用創紀錄的¥15.4兆、即$964億干預匯市，但匯率再次逼近先前觸發美日協同行動的區域。市場反應收窄政策選項：干預可以改變部位，但要持續支撐日圓，愈來愈仰賴國內利率路徑，以及市場對財政政策不會壓過貨幣政策的信心。

最新預算資訊使第二項條件更難達成。18個部會與機構提出的預算要求合計約¥143兆；本年度初始預算加上先前追加預算合計約¥140.6兆。這項數字部分反映首相高市早苗試圖把支出納入常規預算、而非日後追加，因此並非同一口徑下的財政刺激暴增。不過，即使採更廣泛的比較基準，預算要求仍是疫情以來最高，且包括未設上限的成長策略項目，最終預算定案前仍可能增加。日本財務省另要求創紀錄的¥36.6兆償債支出；高市則表示，希望新債發行低於¥40兆。

因此，日本眼前的固定收益張力有三個可觀察面向：升息幾乎已完全反映在定價中，10年期標售在里程碑殖利率附近找到足夠需求，超長端仍須承接一套最終融資尚未解決的財政方案。國內殖利率上升，最終可能鼓勵資金回流，降低日本對海外存續期間的需求；然而日圓未能守住干預成果，顯示這種資產重新配置的力道仍不足以穩定匯率。基準券標售順利，讓3%成為可投資水準；但把貨幣正常化與主權供給一併考量後，市場出清殖利率究竟落在哪裡，仍未定論。

## 緊縮擴大，但各地成長敘事並不一致

歐元區提供了支持再度升息最明確的實際通膨證據。8月整體消費者物價通膨率由2.9%升至3.3%，為近3年最高，足以讓市場完全定價9月10日將存款利率上調25個基點至2.50%。內部指標卻朝相反方向移動：核心通膨由2.5%降至2.4%，服務通膨由3.3%放緩至3.0%。因此，ECB面對的是能源驅動的整體通膨走高，但這份數據並未顯示國內通膨黏性以相同速度加劇。

政策制定者從這種分歧得出不同結論。德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel歡迎核心與服務通膨降溫，並表示未在其中看到二輪效應，儘管他認為短期內的決策方向可以預見。立陶宛的Gediminas Simkus則認為9月升息仍不足夠，理由是天然氣與農產品價格上升，且經濟表現優於預期。市場對未來一年再升息兩次的定價，已超過部分官員與經濟學家認為必要的路徑。9月行動已成共同基本情境；爭議在於能源衝擊是否足以改變中期預測，進而要求政策利率超過估計中性區間的上緣。

英國市場面對的是同一問題的更棘手版本。交易員計入英國央行至2月前升息兩次，英國10年期公債殖利率一度上升11個基點至5.25%，30年期殖利率升至5.89%，為1998年以來最高。Catherine Mann表示成長已增強、勞動市場似乎正在穩定、通膨略高於預期，進一步強化鷹派尾端情境。她的偏好仍具有不對稱性：利率略設過高，日後仍可修正；若容許通膨持續，代價則更大。

房市與信用數據不支持把這種偏好視為委員會已定案的結論。7月房貸核准件數由58,215降至56,053，低於59,400的預期，為2024年1月以來最低。2年期固定房貸平均利率已由戰前的4.83%升至5.59%，把全球能源與利率衝擊直接傳導至家庭融資。Nationwide的8月房價指標上升0.2%至£275,465，略高於0.1%的預期，前值則修正為下跌0.1%；但房貸核准數顯示，房價上升建立在成交量日益萎縮的基礎上。消費者新增£20億無擔保借款，存款增額則由£62億放緩至£38億，顯示家庭正運用資產負債表緩衝能源衝擊造成的所得壓力。

以色列則朝相反方向移動，說明全球緊縮不能一概視為同步週期。以色列央行連續第三次會議降息，將利率由3.50%降至3.25%；調查意見正好各半，十八位經濟學家中有九位預期寬鬆。決策後，以色列謝克爾走弱至1美元兌3.02謝克爾，但仍接近數十年來的強勢水準。通膨已降至目標區間中段附近；剔除以色列企業海外生產後，央行判斷國內活動力道較弱。第2季GDP由戰爭相關萎縮中反彈，年化成長15.4%；但一旦國內通膨與匯率環境騰出空間，即使這項落後指標強勁，也未能阻止央行降息。

巴西則呈現另一種雙向風險。第2季GDP成長0.5%，低於前季的1.1%，但高於0.4%的市場共識；年增2.0%，也高於1.8%的預期。農業成長2.8%，服務業僅成長0.2%，工業成長0.1%，家庭消費萎縮0.4%。14%的Selic利率明顯壓抑利率敏感活動，但8月中通膨仍為4.24%，高於3%目標，選舉前財政支持也持續。優於預期的整體成長降低加快寬鬆的急迫性；消費與製造業疲弱，則使經濟韌性不足以成為重新緊縮的理由。

這些結果共同抬高全球長天期債券殖利率的底部，卻未提供單一政策範本。ECB面對整體通膨上升，同時觀察核心通膨降溫能否延續；英國央行面對價格壓力偏強與房貸傳導明顯轉弱；以色列因匯率與本地通膨騰出空間而能降息，巴西的緊縮性利率則正以不均衡方式發揮作用。即使各經濟體走向不同，全球殖利率仍可維持高檔，因為共同因素不是同步成長榮景，而是市場對輸入型通膨與政策傳導不確定性要求更高溢價。

## 主權融資區分市場准入與困境

主權市場仍能消化龐大融資需求，但各國付出的價格差異甚大。IMF警告，全球公共債務已接近GDP的100%，並高於二戰後高點；核心市場殖利率上升，也提高較弱借款人的外溢風險。G20官員同時仍對全球失衡與主權債務的措辭看法分歧，使會議可能以主席聲明、而非聯合公報收場。缺乏協調並未阻止發債，卻讓各國財政可信度與交易結構更具決定性。

南韓2027年預算為供給面提供具體規模。政府計畫發行222.8兆韓元公債，接近本年度創紀錄的提案規模；其中110.7兆韓元用於再融資到期債務，15.9兆韓元支應做市操作，淨發行約96.3兆韓元。總統李在明為擴張性施政與AI投資工具提供資金，支出預計增加12.8%至820.9兆韓元。3年期殖利率上升6個基點至3.9%，10年期上升9個基點至4.4%。提案仍須國會核准，但已打消市場對年度供給大幅下降的預期。

芬蘭與加拿大顯示，全球賣壓中仍可出現財政分化。芬蘭規劃2027年中央政府赤字€124億，較今年少€9億，並削減€10億支出；然而利息支出增加€12億至€44億，說明即使基本政策方向改善，較高殖利率仍會侵蝕財政整頓成果。加拿大30年期殖利率報4.15%，遠低於美國30年期公債的5.27%，折價幅度也大於過去10年約70個基點的平均值。第2季外資創紀錄買進C$808億加拿大政府債券，有助解釋這種相對韌性；不過，預估C$653億聯邦赤字與新的基礎建設支出，使其財政優勢仍有條件。

沙烏地阿拉伯證明，石油運輸路線遭衝擊時，良好結構仍能動員資本。沙國發行$32.5億的5年期與10年期伊斯蘭債券，訂單高峰超過$150億。10年期券定價為美債殖利率加80個基點，較初步討論水準收窄約30個基點。在荷姆茲附近有油輪遇襲，且沙國經濟正承受石油產業萎縮之際，這筆發行成果格外值得注意。已完成且獲超額認購的債券發行，也不同於規模至少$80億的初步貸款磋商：公開交易證明沙國能按已揭露條件取得資金，貸款則仍只是可能的融資管道。

塞內加爾位於光譜另一端。政府初步敲定$22億IMF計畫，並表示將依改良版G20共同架構尋求債務處理。其歐元計價2028年債券下跌6.9分至49.44分，主權利差由1,651個基點跳升至1,745個基點。先前未揭露債務導致原有$18億融資安排暫停後，IMF協議是一項突破，但也讓債務重組更加明確。該計畫要求矯正措施、對新增外部欠款零容忍，並須執行董事會核准。每年融資需求接近6兆CFA法郎、即$106億；恢復優惠性資金支援可緩解流動性，卻無法消除債券價格目前反映的折讓。

印度面對的是融資錯配，而非困境事件。4月至6月季度，經常帳赤字由一年前修正後的$34億、占GDP 0.4%，擴大至$42億、占GDP 0.5%。商品貿易赤字由$689億增至$861億，國際收支則由$45億盈餘轉為$81億赤字。私人移轉收入由$332億增至$429億，提供部分抵銷；RBI的美元兌盧比折價換匯計畫，預計可吸引外幣存款與債券資金。

Capri Global正從較低信用層級檢驗這項管道。這家非銀行放款機構尋求透過首檔外幣債券籌資$3億至$5億；發行條件為3年3個月期優先擔保債券，初始指引約7.75%，預期評級為BB-。此前較高評級銀行大量發債，令定價失去吸引力，公司因此延後先前一次發行嘗試。6月至8月，印度放款機構在RBI窗口下發行$121.5億美元債，其中逾75%來自民營銀行；單是ICICI Bank便以5.308%完成$5億私募，使其透過該計畫發行的總額達$35.5億。因此，Capri重返市場是在檢驗官方流動性支援能否把離岸市場准入擴展至銀行以外，同時不抹去非銀行風險所需的利差。

兩個較小市場顯示，本地資金池如何降低外部依賴。投資人淡化選後政治緊張，轉而聚焦政策延續、銅價強勢與可能出現的新IMF政策錨定，使尚比亞主權利差由7月30日的216個基點收窄至177個基點；其貨幣今年升值16%，本地債券報酬接近37%。8%的預算赤字與反對派面臨的法律壓力，仍使這份信心帶有保留。烏拉圭披索投資在2年內增至3倍、超過140億披索；2025年3月後，私人存款中的外幣占比由73%降至約69%。截至7月，本地發行額$21億中，固定利率披索證券占逾一半；政府債務的本幣占比也升破57%。這不表示兩國普遍免疫於全球殖利率衝擊，而是證明可信的本幣與制度改革能擴大國內買方基礎。

## 信用平靜掩蓋發行人斷層

與其下方的發行人分化相比，廣泛信用利差依然顯得平靜。約$1兆非金融投資級債券的剩餘到期年限超過3年，交易利差卻相對其評級異常偏寬；其中美國約$5,800億，歐洲近$4,000億。同時，美國高評級債券平均利差接近78個基點，歐洲高評級接近79個基點，都逼近金融危機後最窄水準。週二美國投資級利差小幅擴大、高收益利差擴大較明顯，符合這種格局：指數層級調整有限，產業集中度、發行供給與發行人基本面則決定損失集中在哪裡。

AI融資是造成技術面分化的來源，而非信用體質全面惡化。六大超大規模雲端業者目前約占美國投資級指數的5%，是2年前占比的2倍。JPMorgan Asset Management估計，其低槓桿足以支撐另外$1.5兆債務；三大公司的已簽客戶承諾成長速度也快於資本支出。到2030年，整體基礎建設支出估計達$5.5兆，遠非營運現金流可獨力支應。強健的資產負債表使這些公司仍有能力承擔發債，但指數權重提高，迫使投資人在管理集中度時重新定價其他債券。因此，相對評級偏寬的利差，除了反映預期降評，也可能源於供給與投資組合運作機制。

Brightspeed則是基本面風險直接浮現的案例。這家Apollo支持的寬頻供應商在第2季營收下滑8.7%至$3.86億後，提出繼續經營疑慮警示。上半年公司錄得$8.79億虧損與$3.41億負營運現金流；截至6月30日，仍持有$11.7億現金與$6.77億正營運資金。公司正探索可能包括資產擔保證券化的融資方案，債權人也與顧問合作。光纖業務銷售成長16%，可服務據點超過300萬處，但這些營運進展仍未能覆蓋資本密集的鄉村網路建設成本。先前的困境債務交換減債$11億，並帶來$37億新資金；目前的警示顯示，負債管理仍未解決現金流創造能力問題。

中國Zhongsheng Group透過另一種機制承受墮落天使風險。這家投資級Mercedes-Benz經銷商的2028年美元債自7月以來殖利率一直高於10%，已是投機級債券常見水準，原因是上半年獲利下滑89%。營收下降18.5%，新車銷量下滑17.6%至188,463輛，股價今年下跌約63%。S&P目前給予的評級僅高於高收益級1個級距。流動性仍提供實質緩衝：Zhongsheng持有人民幣136億元現金，足以償付明年到期的$3.5億聯貸與人民幣10億元債券；公司並已回購$1.179億2028年債券，使未償額降至約$4.82億。信用問題在於，這些現金能否協助公司度過豪華車經銷商的結構性壓力，又不被營運資金與再融資消耗。

HDFC Bank債券跌勢範圍較窄，但因該機構規模龐大而具重要性。執行長Sashidhar Jagdishan意外決定不尋求續任後，美元債連續第五個交易日下跌。2031年6月到期債券跌至98.504分，新發行的2029年8月與2031年8月到期債券也觸及最低水準。HDFC占印度存款近12%；其股價今年已下跌約28%，同期Nifty Bank Index僅跌3.3%。Moody's指出，這帶來未預期的領導層交接風險，但若接班有序、策略延續，信用影響仍可受控。與Brightspeed不同，問題不是已揭露的現金耗損，而是治理不確定性可能侵蝕市場對原本強健資產負債表的信心。

中國預售屋改革改變家庭資金流向建商的結構。購屋款如今必須存入信託專戶，工程須封頂後才能開始預售；若逾期交屋，買方有權解約並獲得退款。這項改變保護家庭，卻移除建商一項低成本、期限錯配的融資來源；在適用舊制的建案消化後，2027年新案可能減少。即使成屋銷售已超過新屋，2025年底預售仍約占新屋交易75%。目前系統的曝險低於景氣高峰時期，當時近90%住宅樓地板面積在完工前售出；然而，建商與地方政府仍須承受預收現金減少與土地需求轉弱。

這些案例說明，廣泛利差平靜並不能完整衡量金融情勢。超大規模雲端業者帶來供給與集中度效應，但仍有龐大承擔能力。Brightspeed先前重組未能創造自籌成長資金，目前仍需要融資。Zhongsheng擁有流動性，卻面對結構性轉弱的業務與潛在評級遷移。HDFC的問題是領導層信心，中國房市改革則刻意將完工風險由家庭轉移出去。基準殖利率提高所有發行人的門檻，但固定收益最關鍵的變數，仍是現金流、擔保品、治理與損失究竟落在何處。

## 前瞻市場意涵

接下來的美國數據將判定，通膨色彩濃厚的熊市趨平能否延續到油價衝擊之後。8月ISM服務業指數將於9月3日紐約時間10:00公布，市場共識為54.3，前值54.1。非農就業接著於9月4日08:30公布；市場共識為增加58,000人，前值為減少23,000人，失業率預計維持4.1%。服務價格偏強、就業增幅接近或高於該基準，將支撐市場目前對9月升息機率的定價，並使2至5年期區段持續對另一波通膨意外敏感。就業廣度疲弱或服務業價格降溫，則會把製造業投入成本壓力與全經濟通膨黏性區隔開來，並挑戰前端走勢。

日本與歐元區將透過不同管道，成為下一輪全球存續期間考驗。基準10年期標售在3%附近找到需求後，週四30年期JGB標售必須消化超長券供給；若新券讓利幅度大或投標倍數偏低，將顯示財政不確定性仍集中於銀行與壽險進場天期之外。ECB在9月10日決策時，必須調和3.3%的整體通膨與降溫的核心及服務通膨；日本央行在9月17日至18日會議，則須驗證市場幾近確定的升息定價，或解釋為何日圓疲弱與市場預期強烈仍不足以支持行動。政策如期跟進，將使全球殖利率底部維持高檔；若央行不配合市場預期，則會揭示歐洲與日本殖利率曲線已納入多少緊縮。

美國財政部買回展開前，供給情勢便會變得可觀察。財政部將於9月3日公布9月的3年期、10年期與30年期美債標售規模；市場9月7日因勞動節休市，3年期標售與10年期增額發行接著於9月8日及9日舉行。3年期結果將顯示，政策利率定價上升後能否吸引足夠前端需求；10年期增額發行則檢驗全球重新定價後的存續期間承接能力。投標強勁，將區分總體重新定價與美債市場容量流失。若新券讓利擴大，尤其油價或公司債供給同步增加，則顯示官方流動性支援正與市場持有存續期間風險所要求的價格普遍提高相互競爭。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The oil shock stopped being only a long-end problem and moved directly into the policy-sensitive part of the Treasury curve. The 2-year yield rose 5 basis points to 4.39% and the 5-year climbed 6 basis points to 4.55%, outpacing increases of 4 basis points at 10 years to 4.79% and 2 basis points at 30 years to 5.27%. That bear flattening narrowed 2s10s by 1 basis point to 40 basis points and 2s30s by 3 basis points to 88 basis points. Over the past week, the 2-year has risen 22 basis points against 15 basis points at 10 years and 10 basis points at 30 years. Investors are no longer treating the renewed conflict around the Strait of Hormuz as a distant inflation premium alone; they are assigning it a nearer-term Federal Reserve consequence.

The composition of the move makes that change clear. The 10-year real yield was unchanged at 2.44%, while the 10-year breakeven rose 4 basis points to 2.35%. WTI futures surged 5.83% to $90.76 and Brent gained 5.23% to $95.22 after the United States launched new strikes against Iran, Tehran retaliated, and projectiles hit two tankers attempting to leave the strait. The market therefore marked up inflation compensation without requiring a further rise in the real discount rate at 10 years. A 0.24% increase in the Dollar Index and a 1.21% decline in gold reinforced the role of higher expected policy rates, even though the geopolitical event itself would ordinarily support havens.

Incoming U.S. evidence did not offer the Fed a clean offset. The August ISM manufacturing index remained expansionary at 54.6 but fell from 55.6, missed the 55.2 consensus, and showed new orders slowing to 53.7. Prices paid stayed at an elevated 71.1 and supplier deliveries rose to 59.3, preserving the link from energy, tariffs and supply constraints to near-term inflation risk. Job openings edged up to 7.27 million from 7.18 million, just below the 7.31 million consensus, while Governor Michael Barr said the Fed should act decisively if inflation does not moderate. The combination is not a uniform growth acceleration. It is an uncomfortable mix of slower manufacturing momentum, stable labor demand and persistent input costs that leaves a September hike plausible rather than inevitable.

Risk assets accepted the rates message without displaying systemic stress. The S&P 500 fell 0.71%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 1.29% and the semiconductor index declined 2.14%, while the VIX closed at 16.34. U.S. investment-grade spreads widened modestly, high-yield spreads widened clearly and hard-currency emerging-market spreads widened modestly. That differentiation matters: the selloff impaired duration and lower-quality risk more than it disrupted market functioning. The 30-year yield also remains unchanged over the past month despite its return to 5.27%, limiting the case for an uncontrolled fiscal break. The firmer conclusion is that another oil escalation has converted inflation uncertainty into a broader tightening impulse, and that the front end now needs weaker price or labor evidence to reverse it.

## The Inflation Signal Reaches Policy Tenors

Tuesday's data defined the Fed problem through breadth rather than one headline. Manufacturing activity is still expanding, but the decline in ISM and the 3-point drop in new orders show that the sector is losing speed. At the same time, the unchanged 71.1 prices-paid index is too high to support an uncomplicated disinflation narrative. Respondents cited price volatility and higher costs across aluminum, steel, copper, electrical products, fuel, memory products and semiconductors; shortages were reported in several of the same categories. A rise in supplier-delivery times adds a physical-capacity dimension to the price signal. The slower headline therefore does not carry the policy meaning that a demand-led fall accompanied by easing input costs would have carried.

Other current indicators preserve that ambiguity. The Logistics Managers Index fell to 66.6 from 68.9 but remained firmly expansionary. Redbook same-store sales accelerated to 9.6% year over year from 9.1%, a strong nominal consumption signal, and job openings moved higher even while slightly undershooting expectations. None establishes an overheating economy by itself. Together they show that activity has not deteriorated enough to neutralize an energy shock whose transmission is visible in market inflation compensation.

Barr's intervention added committee breadth to that conclusion. He conditioned patience on evidence that inflation is moderating toward 2%, but made a rate increase the appropriate response if that progress fails. The signal is notable because it came from a governor characterized as relatively centrist and followed three dissents in favor of a hike at the July meeting. Futures consequently assigned close to a 70% probability to a 25-basis-point increase at the September 15-16 meeting. That probability is a market measure, not a policy commitment, and the split between slower new orders and elevated prices explains why roughly 30% of the distribution still favored no change.

Long maturity pricing now carries two related constraints. The 30-year yield at 5.27% has returned to the level immediately before Treasury announced expanded buybacks on August 19, and the 10-year yield is more than 10 basis points higher than it was then. The planned operations, due to begin September 9 and described as at least twice the previous size, can support liquidity in older securities. They cannot by themselves lower the inflation, fiscal or competing-supply compensation required by private holders. Worldwide public debt is approaching 100% of GDP, according to the IMF, while technology companies continue to finance a capital-intensive AI buildout. The present bear flattening says the Fed reaction function is the marginal daily force; the elevated outright level of the long bond says structural absorption has not gone away.

Cross-asset performance sets a useful confidence limit. Semiconductor shares lost more than the broad market as higher discount rates challenged long-duration earnings, and gold extended its decline as the dollar and expected policy path firmed. Yet equity volatility remained contained, and the S&P 500 fell less than 1%. This is a repricing of the cost and distribution of capital, not evidence that financing has shut. The clearer widening in high-yield spreads does show that lower-quality borrowers are becoming more sensitive to the same macro impulse than investment-grade issuers, a distinction that appears more starkly in individual credits than in the broad indexes.

## Japan Clears 3% but Not Its Policy Constraint

Japan's 10-year yield reaching 3% for the first time since 1996 was more than a round-number event. The yield rose as much as 6 basis points and has doubled over roughly a year, while the 2-year reached 1.81%, the 5-year touched a record 2.265%, the 20-year rose to 3.885% and the 30-year approached a record close around 4.18%. This is a curve repricing both a near-term Bank of Japan increase and a larger fiscal compensation requirement. It also changes relative value for banks and life insurers whose funding and liability costs can now be covered by domestic government bonds at yields unavailable for much of the post-1990s period.

The 10-year auction showed that 3% can draw demand without establishing a durable ceiling. Bid-to-cover improved to 3.29 from 2.56 at the prior sale and was close to the 3.26 12-month average. The tail narrowed, and MUFJ Morgan Stanley took 22% of the auction. Those results contrast with the weak 2-year sale in the preceding week and demonstrate that buyers emerged once the average yield approached 3%. The qualification lies in the distribution across the curve: investors still demanded a level above 3% for the benchmark tenor, and the fiscal and duration risk is concentrated more heavily in the 30-year sector ahead of its Thursday auction.

Policy expectations became more forceful during the same window. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's department said after his meeting with Governor Kazuo Ueda that he supported decisive Japanese market and monetary steps to address substantial yen undervaluation, and linked yen weakness to domestic inflation. The readout also emphasized policy communication that anchors inflation expectations and avoids excessive currency volatility. Overnight swaps moved to roughly a 99% probability of a BOJ increase at the September 17-18 meeting, more than twice the probability a month earlier.

Tokyo did not fully accept Washington's characterization. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama denied discussing the conduct of monetary policy with Bessent and stressed the BOJ's institutional authority. The yen nevertheless weakened through 160 per dollar after briefly strengthening on reports of the conversation. Japan had already spent a record ¥15.4 trillion, or $96.4 billion, on intervention during the preceding month, yet the currency again approached the area that triggered coordinated U.S.-Japan action. The market response narrows the policy choice: intervention can alter positioning, but sustained currency support increasingly depends on the domestic rate path and on confidence that fiscal policy will not overwhelm it.

The new budget information makes that second condition harder. Requests from 18 ministries and agencies totaled about ¥143 trillion, compared with roughly ¥140.6 trillion for the current initial budget and the prior supplementary budgets combined. The figure partly reflects Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's attempt to place spending in the regular budget rather than add it later, so it is not a like-for-like surge in fiscal impulse. Even on that broader comparison, however, the request is the largest since the pandemic and contains uncapped growth-strategy items that could increase before the final budget is set. The Finance Ministry is also requesting a record ¥36.6 trillion for debt service, while Takaichi has said she wants new bond issuance below ¥40 trillion.

Japan's immediate fixed-income tension therefore has three observable parts. A policy increase is almost fully discounted, the 10-year auction found acceptable demand at the milestone yield, and the super-long sector still has to absorb a fiscal plan whose final financing is unresolved. Higher domestic yields may eventually encourage repatriation and reduce Japanese demand for foreign duration, but the yen's failure to hold intervention gains shows that this reallocation is not yet powerful enough to stabilize the exchange rate. A smooth benchmark auction has made 3% investable; it has not settled where a market-clearing level lies once monetary normalization and sovereign supply are considered together.

## Tightening Broadens Without a Common Growth Story

The euro area delivered the cleanest realized inflation case for another increase. Headline consumer-price inflation accelerated to 3.3% in August from 2.9%, the highest in almost three years and enough to leave a 25-basis-point increase in the deposit rate to 2.50% on September 10 fully priced. The internal measures moved in the opposite direction: core inflation eased to 2.4% from 2.5%, and services slowed to 3.0% from 3.3%. The ECB therefore confronts a stronger energy-driven headline without evidence in this release that domestic persistence is accelerating at the same pace.

Policymakers drew different implications from that split. Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel welcomed the easing in core and services inflation and said second-round effects were not visible there, even as he described the near-term decision as predictable. Lithuania's Gediminas Simkus argued that the September increase would not be enough, citing higher natural-gas and agricultural-commodity prices and a stronger-than-expected economy. Market pricing for two additional increases over the following year exceeds the path some officials and economists consider necessary. The September step has become the shared base case; the dispute is whether the energy shock changes medium-term projections enough to require policy beyond the upper end of the estimated neutral range.

British markets priced a less comfortable version of the same problem. The 10-year gilt yield rose as much as 11 basis points to 5.25%, and the 30-year reached 5.89%, its highest since 1998, as traders priced two Bank of England increases by February. Catherine Mann reinforced the hawkish tail by saying growth had strengthened, the labor market appeared to be stabilizing and inflation was somewhat firmer than expected. Her preference remains asymmetric: a rate set modestly too high can be corrected later, whereas inflation allowed to persist is more costly.

Housing and credit data argue against treating that preference as a settled committee conclusion. Mortgage approvals fell to 56,053 in July from 58,215 and missed the 59,400 expectation, the lowest total since January 2024. The average 2-year fixed mortgage rate has risen to 5.59% from 4.83% before the war, transmitting the global energy and rates shock directly into household financing. Nationwide's August house-price measure rose 0.2% to £275,465, slightly above the 0.1% expectation and after a revised 0.1% decline, but approvals suggest the price result rests on a thinning transaction base. Consumers borrowed an additional £2 billion unsecured while deposits slowed to £3.8 billion from £6.2 billion, consistent with households using balance sheets to smooth an energy-related income squeeze.

Israel moved in the opposite direction and showed why global tightening cannot be reduced to a synchronized cycle. The Bank of Israel cut its rate for a third consecutive meeting, to 3.25% from 3.50%, after an evenly split survey in which nine of 18 economists expected easing. The shekel weakened to 3.02 per dollar after the decision but remained near multi-decade strength. Inflation has moderated toward the middle of the target range, and the central bank judged domestic activity less forceful after excluding production abroad by Israeli firms. Second-quarter GDP had rebounded at a 15.4% annualized rate from a war-related contraction, but that backward-looking strength did not prevent a cut once local inflation and currency conditions created room.

Brazil adds a different kind of two-way risk. GDP expanded 0.5% in Q2, down from 1.1% but above the 0.4% consensus, and grew 2.0% from a year earlier against a 1.8% expectation. Agriculture rose 2.8%, while services grew only 0.2%, industry 0.1% and household consumption contracted 0.4%. A 14% Selic rate is clearly restraining rate-sensitive activity, yet mid-August inflation at 4.24% remains above the 3% target and fiscal support continues ahead of the election. Better-than-expected headline growth reduces the urgency of faster easing; weaker consumption and manufacturing prevent resilience from becoming a case for renewed tightening.

These outcomes place a common floor under global duration without supplying one policy template. The ECB is responding to a higher headline while testing whether core disinflation persists. The BOE faces firm prices and a visibly weaker mortgage channel. Israel can ease because its currency and local inflation create room, while Brazil's restrictive setting is biting unevenly. Global yields can remain elevated even when these economies move in different directions, because the unifying factor is a higher premium for uncertainty about imported inflation and policy transmission rather than a shared growth boom.

## Sovereign Funding Separates Access From Distress

The sovereign market is clearing large funding needs, but at sharply different prices. The IMF warned that worldwide public debt is close to 100% of GDP and above post-World War II highs, with rising core-market yields increasing the spillover risk for weaker borrowers. G20 officials simultaneously remained divided over language on global imbalances and sovereign debt, raising the possibility that the meeting would end with a chair's statement rather than a joint communique. That lack of coordination does not prevent issuance; it makes national fiscal credibility and transaction structure more decisive.

South Korea's 2027 budget gives the supply side a concrete scale. The government plans gross bond issuance of 222.8 trillion won, close to the current year's record proposal. Of that amount, 110.7 trillion won would refinance maturing debt and 15.9 trillion won would support market-making operations, leaving about 96.3 trillion won of net issuance. Spending is projected to rise 12.8% to 820.9 trillion won as President Lee Jae Myung funds an expansionary agenda and an AI investment vehicle. The 3-year yield rose 6 basis points to 3.9% and the 10-year climbed 9 basis points to 4.4%. The proposal still requires parliamentary approval, but it already removes expectations for a much larger decline in annual supply.

Finland and Canada show that fiscal differentiation remains possible inside the global selloff. Finland plans a €12.4 billion central-government deficit in 2027, €0.9 billion less than this year, alongside €1 billion of spending cuts. Yet interest expenditure rises by €1.2 billion to €4.4 billion, illustrating how higher yields can consume consolidation even when the primary policy direction improves. Canada's 30-year yield stood at 4.15%, well below the 5.27% U.S. long bond and at a wider discount than its roughly 70-basis-point average over the past decade. Record second-quarter foreign purchases of C$80.8 billion in Canadian government bonds help explain that relative resilience, although a projected C$65.3 billion federal deficit and new infrastructure spending keep the fiscal advantage conditional.

Saudi Arabia demonstrated that strong structure can still mobilize capital during an oil-route shock. The kingdom sold $3.25 billion of 5- and 10-year sukuk, attracting orders that peaked above $15 billion. The 10-year tranche priced 80 basis points over Treasuries, about 30 basis points tighter than initial discussion. That execution is notable while tankers are being struck near Hormuz and the Saudi economy is absorbing an oil-sector contraction. It also distinguishes a completed, oversubscribed bond sale from preliminary talks for at least an $8 billion loan: the public transaction shows access at disclosed terms, whereas the loan remains a possible funding channel.

Senegal occupies the opposite end of the spectrum. The government agreed on a preliminary $2.2 billion IMF program and said it would pursue a debt treatment under an improved version of the G20 Common Framework. Its euro-denominated 2028 bond fell 6.9 cents to 49.44 cents, and the sovereign spread jumped to 1,745 basis points from 1,651. The IMF agreement is a breakthrough after undisclosed debt caused suspension of a previous $1.8 billion facility, but it also makes restructuring more explicit. The program requires corrective measures, zero tolerance for new external arrears and executive-board approval. With annual financing needs near 6 trillion CFA francs, or $10.6 billion, renewed concessional support can ease liquidity without eliminating the concessions now embedded in bond prices.

India presents a funding mismatch rather than a distress event. The current-account deficit widened to $4.2 billion, or 0.5% of GDP, in the April-June quarter from a revised $3.4 billion, or 0.4%, a year earlier. The merchandise deficit expanded to $86.1 billion from $68.9 billion, and the balance of payments moved to an $8.1 billion deficit from a $4.5 billion surplus. Private transfers increased to $42.9 billion from $33.2 billion, providing an offset, while RBI programs using discounted dollar-rupee swaps are expected to attract foreign-currency deposits and bond funding.

Capri Global is testing that channel at a lower credit tier. The non-bank lender sought $300 million to $500 million through its first foreign-currency bond, a 3-year-and-3-month senior secured note with initial guidance around 7.75% and an expected BB- rating. It had delayed an earlier attempt when heavy, higher-rated bank supply made pricing unattractive. Indian lenders raised $12.15 billion in dollar bonds from June through August under the RBI window, more than 75% from private-sector banks; ICICI Bank alone completed a $500 million private placement at 5.308%, taking its issuance under the program to $3.55 billion. Capri's return therefore tests whether official liquidity support can broaden offshore access beyond banks without erasing the spread demanded for non-bank risk.

Two smaller markets show how local capital pools can reduce external dependence. Zambia's sovereign spread narrowed to 177 basis points from 216 on July 30, its currency strengthened 16% this year and local bonds returned almost 37%, as investors looked through post-election political tensions toward policy continuity, copper strength and a possible new IMF anchor. An 8% budget deficit and legal pressure on the opposition keep that confidence qualified. Uruguay's peso investments tripled over two years to more than 14 billion pesos, while the foreign-currency share of private deposits fell to about 69% from 73% after March 2025. Fixed-rate peso securities accounted for more than half of $2.1 billion in domestic issuance through July, and the local-currency share of government debt rose above 57%. These are not broad immunity from the global yield shock; they are evidence that credible local currency and institutional reform can widen the domestic buyer base.

## Credit Calm Conceals Issuer Fault Lines

Broad credit spreads still look placid relative to the dispersion underneath. Roughly $1 trillion of non-financial investment-grade bonds with more than 3 years to maturity trade unusually wide for their ratings, including about $580 billion in the United States and nearly $400 billion in Europe. At the same time, average U.S. high-grade spreads stand near 78 basis points and European high-grade near 79 basis points, close to post-crisis tights. Tuesday's modest widening in U.S. investment grade and clearer move in high yield fit that pattern: the index-level adjustment is limited, while sector concentration, issuance and issuer fundamentals determine where losses accumulate.

AI financing is one source of technical dispersion rather than a universal credit deterioration. The six largest hyperscalers now represent roughly 5% of the U.S. investment-grade index, twice their share 2 years ago. JPMorgan Asset Management estimates that their low leverage could support another $1.5 trillion of debt and notes that signed customer commitments at the three largest companies are growing faster than capital spending. The broader infrastructure bill is estimated at $5.5 trillion by 2030, far beyond what operating cash flow alone can fund. Strong balance sheets keep issuance serviceable, but their growing index weights force other bonds to reprice as investors manage concentration. A wide spread relative to rating can therefore reflect supply and portfolio mechanics as well as an anticipated downgrade.

Brightspeed supplies a case where the fundamental risk is direct. The Apollo-backed broadband provider added a going-concern warning after second-quarter revenue fell 8.7% to $386 million. It recorded an $879 million loss and $341 million of negative operating cash flow in the first half, despite holding $1.17 billion of cash and $677 million of positive working capital at June 30. The company is exploring financing that could include an asset-backed securitization while creditors work with advisers. Fiber sales grew 16% and enabled locations exceeded 3 million, but those operating gains have not yet covered the cost of a capital-intensive rural network build. A prior distressed exchange reduced debt by $1.1 billion and brought $3.7 billion of new capital; the current warning shows that liability management did not resolve the cash-generation problem.

China's Zhongsheng Group carries fallen-angel risk through a different mechanism. The investment-grade Mercedes-Benz dealer's 2028 dollar bond has yielded more than 10% since July, a level associated with speculative-grade debt, after first-half profit fell 89%. Revenue declined 18.5%, new-vehicle volume dropped 17.6% to 188,463 units and the shares lost about 63% this year. S&P already rates the company one notch above high yield. Liquidity provides a meaningful cushion: Zhongsheng held 13.6 billion yuan in cash, enough to cover a $350 million syndicated loan and a 1 billion yuan bond due next year, and it repurchased $117.9 million of the 2028 note, leaving about $482 million outstanding. The credit question is whether that cash can bridge a structural squeeze on luxury dealerships without being consumed by working capital and refinancing.

HDFC Bank's bond decline is narrower but significant because of the institution's scale. Dollar notes fell for a fifth session after Chief Executive Officer Sashidhar Jagdishan unexpectedly decided not to seek reappointment. The June 2031 bond dropped to 98.504 cents, and newly issued August 2029 and 2031 notes reached their lowest levels. HDFC accounts for nearly 12% of India's deposits, and its shares have fallen about 28% this year against a 3.3% decline in the Nifty Bank Index. Moody's described an unanticipated leadership-transition risk but said orderly succession and strategic continuity could contain the credit effect. Unlike Brightspeed, the issue is not disclosed cash depletion; it is the risk that governance uncertainty erodes confidence in a fundamentally strong balance sheet.

China's reform of home pre-sales changes the structure through which household cash reaches developers. Buyer payments must now be held in escrow, pre-sales can begin only after construction has topped out, and a missed delivery date gives the buyer a right to terminate the contract and receive a refund. The change protects households but removes a source of cheap, maturity-mismatched funding for developers and may reduce new projects in 2027 after the grandfathered pipeline runs down. Pre-sales still accounted for about 75% of new-home transactions at the end of 2025, even though existing-home sales have overtaken new homes. The immediate system is less exposed than it would have been at the boom's peak, when almost 90% of residential floor space was pre-sold, but developers and local governments will still absorb lower advance cash and weaker land demand.

These cases explain why broad spread calm is an incomplete measure of financial conditions. Hyperscalers create supply and concentration effects while retaining substantial capacity. Brightspeed needs financing after an earlier restructuring failed to produce self-funded growth. Zhongsheng has liquidity but faces a structurally weaker business and potential rating migration. HDFC's issue is leadership confidence, and China's property reform deliberately reallocates completion risk away from households. Benchmark yields raise the hurdle for all of them, but the decisive fixed-income variable remains the location of cash flow, collateral, governance and loss.

## Forward Market Significance

U.S. data must now determine whether the inflation-heavy bear flattening survives beyond the oil shock. The August ISM services index arrives September 3 at 10:00 a.m. New York time, with a 54.3 consensus against 54.1 previously. Payrolls follow September 4 at 8:30 a.m.; the consensus centers on a 58,000 gain after a 23,000 decline, with unemployment expected to remain at 4.1%. Firm services prices and hiring near or above that profile would leave the market's September-hike probability supported and keep the 2- to 5-year sector sensitive to another inflation surprise. Weak employment breadth or an easing in service-sector prices would separate manufacturing input pressure from economy-wide persistence and challenge the front-end move.

Japan and the euro area provide the next global-duration tests through different channels. Thursday's 30-year JGB auction must place super-long supply after the benchmark 10-year sale found demand near 3%; a large concession or weak coverage would show that fiscal uncertainty remains concentrated beyond the maturity where banks and insurers stepped in. The ECB's September 10 decision then has to reconcile a 3.3% headline rate with easing core and services inflation, while the BOJ's September 17-18 meeting must either validate near-certain hike pricing or explain why a weak yen and strong market expectations do not yet justify action. Policy follow-through would keep the global yield floor elevated; pushback would expose how much tightening is already embedded in European and Japanese curves.

U.S. supply becomes observable before the buybacks begin. Treasury announces sizes for the September 3-year, 10-year and 30-year operations on September 3, the market closes for Labor Day on September 7, and the 3-year auction and 10-year reopening follow on September 8 and 9. The 3-year result will show whether higher policy-rate pricing attracts enough front-end demand, while the 10-year reopening tests duration absorption after the global reset. Strong bidding would distinguish a macro repricing from a loss of Treasury market capacity. Larger concessions, especially alongside another rise in oil or corporate issuance, would show that official liquidity support is competing with a broader increase in the price required to warehouse duration.

section_summaries.next_check: Thursday's 30-year auction must show whether demand extends beyond the benchmark without a large concession.
section_summaries.section_title: Japan Clears 3% but Not Its Policy Constraint
section_summaries.summary: Japan's 10-year yield reached 3% and drew a 3.29 bid-to-cover, but the yen weakened through 160 per dollar even as a BOJ increase became roughly 99% priced. Budget requests near ¥143 trillion and the pending 30-year auction leave super-long fiscal absorption—not benchmark demand—as the unresolved constraint.

section_summaries.market_read: Imported-inflation uncertainty is lifting the global duration floor even though local growth and policy paths are diverging.
section_summaries.next_check: ECB projections must show whether the energy-led headline rise is broadening into persistence beyond the September increase.
section_summaries.section_title: Tightening Broadens Without a Common Growth Story
section_summaries.summary: Euro-area headline inflation rose to 3.3% as core and services eased, fully pricing a September 10 ECB increase; UK rate expectations hardened despite weaker mortgage approvals, Israel cut to 3.25%, and Brazil's 0.5% growth beat masked contracting consumption under a 14% Selic rate.

section_summaries.market_read: Access remains available, but investors are separating liquidity support from solvency and rewarding credible domestic funding bases.
section_summaries.next_check: Capri's attempted debut pricing will show whether RBI-backed dollar liquidity reaches beyond banks without erasing the premium for non-bank risk.
section_summaries.section_title: Sovereign Funding Separates Access From Distress
section_summaries.summary: Large funding needs are clearing at prices set by credibility and structure: South Korea plans 222.8 trillion won of gross issuance, Finland's smaller deficit is offset by higher interest expense, Canada retains foreign-backed relative resilience, and Saudi Arabia's $3.25 billion sukuk was heavily oversubscribed. Senegal's $2.2 billion IMF accord formalizes restructuring risk, while India's external gap and Capri's debut test offshore access; Zambia and Uruguay show how local-currency buyer bases can reduce external dependence.

section_summaries.market_read: Benchmark calm understates how higher yields are exposing cash-flow, concentration, governance and collateral weaknesses issuer by issuer.
section_summaries.next_check: Brightspeed's financing structure and Zhongsheng's cash use will show whether current dispersion converts into default or downgrade risk.
section_summaries.section_title: Credit Calm Conceals Issuer Fault Lines
section_summaries.summary: Near-tight high-grade indexes conceal roughly $1 trillion of bonds trading wide for their ratings. Hyperscaler supply creates concentration pressure, Brightspeed's going-concern warning follows $341 million of negative first-half operating cash flow, Zhongsheng pairs liquidity with fallen-angel risk, HDFC faces succession uncertainty, and China's escrow reform removes cheap developer funding.

section_summaries.market_read: Macro persistence, sovereign absorption and central-bank follow-through now determine whether the selloff broadens or unwinds.
section_summaries.next_check: The September 3 ISM services release is the first test of whether firm prices extend beyond manufacturing into the broader economy.
